survivors.why: Removing `frozen=True` from KeptFigure only allows assigning to its fields afterwards. Nothing assigns to a KeptFigure: plan() builds it once and hands it on, and the sibling classes in this file carry the same line. No state exists in which what is written, stored or said differs.

survivors.line: if column == "settlement" and name in only_a_fee:
survivors.why: The test only decides whether `fee_base_was` is set. `fee_base_was` is read only inside `if fee_keys and not fee_seen`, and `fee_keys` is empty for any row that is not in `only_a_fee`. Changing the test therefore changes a value that is never read in the rows it newly applies to (PR1c).

survivors.line: def _a_note_in_the_logs_folder(transport, inside: str) -> Callable[[str, str], None]:
survivors.why: No check reaches nightly's wiring of the before-history note onto the real Drive transport: it is one call to the already proven `_put_in_place` into the Logs folder. The callback the ledger calls is checked with a stand-in in ledger_sheet_checks (name, text, one note per file). First live night shows it. Weaker than the other reasons (PR1c).

Same function as the entry above: returning the note-keeping callback. Without it nightly would pass no callback and the before-history lines would be said in the log but no note file kept. No check reaches nightly's real Drive wiring; the callback itself is checked in ledger_sheet_checks. Weaker than the other reasons (PR1c).

survivors.line: if unwrapped is not body and landing.what_it_really_is(unwrapped) != landing.ZIP:
survivors.why: The second half of a defensive condition: the landing's unwrapper returns a spreadsheet, and an inner plain zip is refused by the reader's next step in words anyway. Not shown unreachable by a check; the first half is killed by the zip-with-one-spreadsheet checks (PR1 A4).
